groups.name: TV shows centred on addiction as a primary dramatic engine
groups.explanation: Nurse Jackie (Edie Falco as an opioid-addicted ER nurse), Weeds (Nancy Botwin's marijuana dealing spirals into addiction-adjacent chaos), Euphoria (teen drug addiction in suburban America), and Intervention (A&E documentary series following people in the grip of addiction toward a staged intervention) all place addiction at the absolute centre of their dramatic premise.

groups.name: TV series whose entire run was revealed to be a dream or fantasy in the finale
groups.explanation: Newhart (1990 finale: Dick Loudon wakes up as Bob Hartley revealing the whole Newhart run was a dream), St. Elsewhere (1988 finale: the entire series is revealed to exist inside an autistic boy's snow-globe fantasy), Dallas (1986: the entire Season 9 was revealed to be Pam Ewing's dream, bringing Bobby back to life), and Roseanne (1997 finale: Roseanne reveals the final season was her own fiction she wrote after Dan's death) are the four most famous examples of a TV series using a dream or fantasy reveal to reframe its entire run.

groups.name: Crime dramas set in a specific small, tight-knit community where everyone knows everyone
groups.explanation: Mare of Easttown (working-class suburb of Easttown, Pennsylvania), Rectify (Paulie, Georgia, a tiny Southern town where Daniel Holden's case ripples through every relationship), Bloodline (the Florida Keys Rayburn family dynasty in an inescapably small island community), and The Killing (Seattle's tight neighbourhoods and a single school community in Season 1) all derive their tension from crimes playing out inside insular communities where characters cannot escape one another.

groups.name: Shows where the primary dramatic set piece is a psychologically intense face-to-face interview between investigator and killer
groups.explanation: Mindhunter (FBI agents Douglas and Tench conduct long-form psychological interviews with incarcerated serial killers as the show's structural spine), The Fall (DSI Stella Gibson's cat-and-mouse psychological confrontations with Paul Spector build across seasons to a direct face-to-face reckoning), Hannibal (Will Graham and later Clarice-role characters conduct intimate psychological interviews with Dr. Lecter that are the show's dramatic heart), and Criminal: UK (the entire show takes place inside a single interview room where detectives face suspects in real time) are all defined by the sustained, psychologically charged face-to-face interview between investigator and killer as their central dramatic device.
